subject: ggplot2_0.9.0: No legend when a second data frame is used

messages.author: a8b98878fdaec163
messages.subject: ggplot2_0.9.0: No legend when a second data frame is used
parts:
Hi all,

The new ggplot2 seems to suppress the legend when the scales come from
a second data set. In the following example, I used to get a legend,
but it is suppressed now. How can I force the legend to be generated?
Thanks.


mtcar_means <- ddply(mtcars, .(cyl), summarise, mpg = mean(mpg))
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=disp, y=mpg)) + geom_point() +
geom_hline(aes(yintercept=mpg, colour=factor(cyl)),
data=mtcar_means)


Wayne

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2_0.9.0: No legend when a second data frame is used
parts:
On 4/6/2012 12:09 PM, Wayne Zhang wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> The new ggplot2 seems to suppress the legend when the scales come from
> a second data set. In the following example, I used to get a legend,
> but it is suppressed now. How can I force the legend to be generated?
> Thanks.
>
>
> mtcar_means<- ddply(mtcars, .(cyl), summarise, mpg = mean(mpg))
> ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=disp, y=mpg)) + geom_point() +
> geom_hline(aes(yintercept=mpg, colour=factor(cyl)),
> data=mtcar_means)
>
>
> Wayne

Actually, it is not the second data set, it is the defaults of
geom_hline that have changed. What you want is:

data=mtcar_means, show_guide=TRUE)

By way of showing it is not the second data set, this uses a second data
set and does have a legend

geom_point(aes(x=200, y=mpg, colour=factor(cyl)),
data=mtcar_means)

And this uses the same data set and doesn't have a legend:

geom_hline(aes(yintercept=mpg, colour=factor(cyl)))


--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University
